slot.brief: Give two octahedral complexes (one with weak-field, one with strong-field ligand); compare unpaired electrons and spin-only magnetic moments.

stem: For octahedral $A=[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ and $B=[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_6]^{4-}$, choose $(n_A,\mu_A; n_B,\mu_B)$, where $n$ is the number of unpaired electrons and $\mu$ is the spin-only magnetic moment.

verdicts.working: Fe²⁺ is d⁶. H₂O gives high-spin octahedral d⁶ with 4 unpaired electrons, so μ = √[4(4+2)] = 4.90 B.M. CN⁻ gives low-spin d⁶ with 0 unpaired electrons and μ = 0.

working:
$\text{Fe}^{2+}: d^6$ in both complexes.
$\text{H}_2\text{O}$: weak field, high spin, $n_A=4$.
$\text{CN}^-$: strong field, low spin, $n_B=0$.
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\ \text{B.M.}$
$\mu_A=\sqrt{24}=4.90\ \text{B.M.},\quad \mu_B=0$.

Independent check: Fe²⁺ is d⁶. H₂O gives high-spin octahedral d⁶ with 4 unpaired electrons, so μ = √[4(4+2)] = 4.90 B.M. CN⁻ gives low-spin d⁶ with 0 unpaired electrons and μ = 0.
solution:
Both complexes contain $\text{Fe}^{2+}$, which is $d^6$. In an octahedral field, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ gives high-spin $d^6$ ($n_A=4$), while $\text{CN}^-$ gives low-spin $d^6$ ($n_B=0$).
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}\ \text{B.M.},\qquad \mu_A=\sqrt{24}=4.90\ \text{B.M.},\quad \mu_B=0.$$
